subject: extracting data frm a Shiny object - splitting a csv read object

messages.author: 5117fd6c9c423ce1
messages.subject: extracting data frm a Shiny object - splitting a csv read object
parts:
taking my earlier example a bit further, is there a reason why this does not work for me:

 mydata <- reactive({
    inFile <- input$file1
   
    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)
    return(
    read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep, quote=input$quote)
    )
    })
   
   
# 'split' the data, in case we have 2 groups in the dataset
  datalist <- split(mydata(), mydata()$group)  


I get the following error from the datalist assignment:

Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() : 
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive function.)

Is there a workaround?  Or am I doing something wrong.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: extracting data frm a Shiny object - splitting a csv read object
parts:
If that split call is happening directly inside of your server function, and not inside another reactive() or a renderXXX call, then it's indeed wrong. You're asking to access mydata, which is reactive, but you're not running in a context that is itself reactive; put another way, you've asked for the value and to be notified about changes to the value in the future yet you've called it in a way that makes it impossible for you to be notified in the future.

In this case, if this error didn't exist, the call would succeed but the value would be NULL 100% of the time (since it occurs as the session is starting up, before the user has given us any input) and would never change from NULL.

So either make a new reactive expression that represents the split data [ datalist <- reactive(split(mydata(), mydata()$group)) ] or do the splitting directly in your renderPlot or whatever if you don't need that data from more than one place.
